scenes.title: Three Hours Early
scenes.summary: At twelve noon on Saturday, F1 answers a telephone call from the station announcing that the retired mapmaker arrives at three in the afternoon instead of six.
scenes.intro: Twelve noon strikes on Saturday at {SHOW}. {F1} picks up the ringing black telephone at the front desk while {M2} straightens his jacket lapel and {M1} checks the room ledger. Listen first.
story: F1
Good afternoon, {SHOW} in {CITY}, {F1} speaking—how may I help you today?
M2
Who is calling at noon, {F1}? Is another neighbour asking for a courtyard seat?
F1
Yes, operator, read the station telegram slowly... arriving on the early express at THREE?!
M1
Three in the afternoon?! Wait—the anniversary tea is scheduled for six this evening!
F1
Thank you very much for calling ahead—goodbye! Gentlemen, put down your teacups!
M2
Did you just say our guest of honour arrives three full hours early?!
F1
Track repair moved his evening connection onto the fast afternoon express into {CITY}!
M2
Three hours left! The cakes are still batter, and the duet is half rehearsed!
M1
Take one deep breath, boss, before you lose the glasses sitting on your nose.
F1
First job: I sprint to the kitchen so {F2} heats both ovens right now!
M1
Second job: {M2}, send quick word down {STREET} inviting neighbours for half past three.
M2
Wait—right after I checked in Rooms Two and Six, where did their keys go?!
scenes.outro: Three hours vanish in a single telephone call—and {M2} has just noticed something strange on the wooden key board! See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Cakes by Half Past Two
scenes.summary: F1 bursts into the café kitchen with the early-train news, and F2 and M4 launch a high-speed relay to bake and cool four berry-and-almond cakes before three.
scenes.intro: Ten seconds later in the warm café kitchen, {F2} and {M4} are calmly shelling almonds when {F1} rushes through the swinging door holding up three fingers. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
Emergency bulletin from the station desk: our mapmaker arrives at three sharp today!
F2
Three in the afternoon?! {M4}, turn both ovens up to baking heat this second!
M4
Both switches on! How fast can four berry almond cakes bake AND cool, {F2}?
F2
Forty minutes in the oven, thirty minutes to cool, ten minutes for warm honey glaze!
F1
That brings us to twenty-five past two—with thirty-five minutes to spare!
M4
I will grease all four round tins with butter while you whisk the eggs, {F2}!
F2
{F1}, rinse those four bowls of fresh summer berries and pat them dry with linen!
F1
Rinsing fast and gentle! Thank goodness we tested all three glazes on Sunday!
M4
Imagine serving Batch One brass polish or Batch Two roof tiles at three today!
F2
Less joking and faster whisking, {M4}—fold the ground almonds in smoothly!
F1
Wait—hear {M1} calling my name from the lobby? Something happened with the room keys!
F2
Go save the front desk, {F1}; {M4} and I own this kitchen until half past two!
scenes.outro: Both ovens roar to life in {F2} and {M4}'s capable hands while {F1} dashes back to solve a front-desk key mystery. See you next time.

scenes.title: Keys Two and Six Swapped
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M1 proves from his paper ledger that M2 accidentally handed Room 2's key to Room 6 and Room 6's key to Room 2 while wearing his glasses on his forehead.
scenes.intro: Back at the front desk, {M1} points his carpenter pencil at two empty brass hooks on the wooden board while {M2} blinks at his forehead and {F1} skids to a stop. Listen first.
story: F1
Report, {M1}! Which room keys went sideways during the noon telephone call?
M1
Look at my paper book: two young hikers booked Room Two on the first floor.
M2
Yes, lovely polite hikers—and a quiet lady with a floral hatbox booked Room Six!
M1
Now tell {F1} where your glasses were when you handed out tags Two and Six.
M2
Oh dear... upside down, two becomes five, no—two and six look remarkably similar blurry!
F1
Did the hikers take backpacks to Room Six while the hatbox went to Room Two?!
M1
Lucky for you, boss, both guests dropped their bags outside the doors and went for lunch!
F1
Really?! Neither guest unlocked the wrong room or unpacked a single shirt yet?!
M1
I passed them at the gate two minutes ago asking where to buy noon soup.
M2
{M1}, your eyes are worth their weight in gold—can we move the bags right now?
F1
And leave clean welcome notes on each door table explaining the right hook number!
M1
Grab the master ring, {F1}; you take the hatbox, and I have the two backpacks.
scenes.outro: Thanks to lunch soup down {STREET}, {F1} and {M1} have fifteen minutes to put every bag at the right door! See you upstairs next time.

scenes.title: Backpacks and a Hatbox
scenes.summary: In the upstairs hallway, F3 steps out of Room 4 to help F1 and M1 guide the swapped hallway bags to their proper doors with cheerful welcome cards.
scenes.intro: Up on the bright carpeted landing, {F1} carries a round striped hatbox toward Room 6 while {M1} shoulders two green hiking backpacks down toward Room 2—just as {F3} opens the door of Room 4 with sheet music in hand. Listen first.
story: F3
Well, hello! Are we playing musical chairs with guest luggage before the concert?
F1
{M2} checked in two rooms without his glasses right before the early-train call, {F3}!
F3
Did you say EARLY train?! What time is our honoured mapmaker arriving today?!
M1
Three sharp this afternoon, madam—three hours ahead of the printed card.
F3
Good heavens! {M3} and I have not finished rehearsing the middle bridge of our duet!
F1
Do not worry, {F3}; here sits the striped hatbox safe and sound outside Room Six!
M1
And both green backpacks are parked neatly on the bench beside Room Two.
F3
Let me write two polite calligraphy cards so the guests swap brass tags at the desk.
F1
Oh, thank you, {F3}—your handwriting makes even a key mix-up look five-star!
M1
Tuck one card on hook two, one card on hook six, problem solved before one.
F3
Now tell me where {M3} is hiding—we need thirty solid minutes at that walnut piano!
F1
He just walked through the courtyard gate—meet him inside Room Nine right now!
scenes.outro: Luggage is sorted, calligraphy cards are placed, and the relay baton passes straight to the piano bench in Room 9! See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Hands at One Piano
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, F3 coaches M3 through their joyful four-hand piano duet, helping the careful architect trade strict counting for warm musical flow.
scenes.intro: At half past one inside sunlit Room 9, {F3} slides right on the long walnut piano bench so {M3} can take the bass keys on the left for their four-hand welcome duet. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M3
Three sharp, {F3}—my hands have not played four-hand piano since I was twelve!
F3
Your left hand remembers every chord, {M3}; just stop counting bars like brick walls!
M3
Sorry! Habit of an architect: one-two-three, four-point-zero metres to the window!
F3
Think of our courtyard tree swaying gently in Friday wind instead of a ruler.
M3
All right, deep breath... bass chord C, warm G, up to A minor...
F3
Lovely! Hear how rich the lower walnut strings sound beneath my melody on top?
M3
Watch out—here comes that fast turn at bar sixteen where I always rush!
F3
Listen to my right hand breathe first, then step in like an old friend answering.
M3
One, two, step in... hey, middle D sang right between our hands without a hitch!
F3
Bravo, {M3}! Your old cartography professor is going to beam from ear to ear!
M3
Wait—look out the arched window: {F2} and {M4} are carrying four hot tins outside!
F3
One more run from the top, partner, while the summer berry cakes cool in the shade!
scenes.outro: Bass chords and bright treble blend smoothly through the open green shutters as four golden cakes emerge into the courtyard! See you next time.

scenes.title: Cooling Tins in the Shade
scenes.summary: At two-fifteen under the courtyard shade tree, F2, M4, and F1 cool the four golden cakes in the breeze and brush on the warm honey-orange glaze.
scenes.intro: Quarter past two in the leafy shade under the courtyard tree! {F2} and {M4} set four fragrant golden cakes onto raised wire racks while {F1} brings out bowls of warm wildflower honey and grated orange peel. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Four golden cakes out of the oven without a single cracked top, Chef!
F2
Feel this gentle shaded breeze under the tree—nature built us a cooling fan!
F1
The whole courtyard smells like roasted almonds, ripe berries, and sweet summer sun!
F2
Touch the side of tin one lightly, {M4}—is it warm rather than piping hot?
M4
Just warm to the palm, {F2}—ready for the thirty-year secret glaze!
F1
Here is the warm honey whisked with sweet orange zest and two pastry brushes!
F2
Brush gently from the centre outward so every berry shines like polished ruby glass.
M4
And {F1} scatters the toasted almond flakes right across the golden top!
F1
Look at our twenty-eight birch clothespins holding every white napkin steady on the tables!
F2
Wait—what time does the courtyard clock say right now, {M4}?
M4
Twenty-eight minutes past two! My brother and I should walk to Central Station now!
F1
Apron off, {M4}—I drew a brass compass welcome sign for you at the gate!
scenes.outro: Four ruby-and-gold cakes glisten in the shade with thirty minutes left on the clock as {M4} races for the station! See you at the gate next time.

scenes.title: Off to the Station Platform
scenes.summary: At half past two by the street gate, F1 hands M3 and M4 a compass-rose welcome card so the two brothers can greet the retired mapmaker at Central Station.
scenes.intro: At half past two under the stone archway of the front gate, {F1} hands a crisp cream welcome sign bearing an eight-point compass rose to {M3} and {M4}. Listen first.
story: F1
Here is your station sign, gentlemen: Welcome Back to Room Eight and Room Nine!
M3
Look, {M4}—{F1} even drew that exact eight-point compass rose in the corner!
M4
Platform three arrives in twenty minutes, little brother, and the station walk takes twelve.
M3
Will he even remember me from a crowded university lecture hall ten years ago?
F1
Are you kidding, {M3}? You recognized his tiny ink star inside one second!
M4
Besides, teachers never forget the quiet student who measures every room in his notebook.
F1
Help carry his suitcase from the platform and take a station taxi straight back here!
M3
Did {M2} manage to invite the neighbours down {STREET} for half past three?
F1
Sixteen neighbours already replied yes, and number ten is tuning his violin right now!
M4
Save two seats near the piano for us—come on, {M3}, eyes forward and no shortcuts!
M3
Definitely zero {M2} alleys today—straight down {STREET} to Central Station!
F1
Ring the gate bell twice when your taxi pulls up at three!
scenes.outro: Two brothers stride side by side down {STREET} toward Central Station while {SHOW} prepares its warmest welcome. One final scene for Episode 5!

scenes.title: Footsteps Outside the Gate
scenes.summary: At three sharp in the glowing courtyard, M2 checks his glasses on his nose, F2 sets hot mint tea on table one, and the gate bell rings twice as a taxi arrives.
scenes.intro: Two minutes to three at {SHOW}! Rooftop lanterns sway gently above twenty-eight clipped linen settings, four summer berry cakes gleam on white stands, and {F1}, {F2}, and {M2} gather near the open courtyard gate. Listen first.
story: M2
Quick check before three strikes: jacket buttoned, shoes polished—where are my glasses?!
F1
Miracle of miracles, {M2}, they are sitting squarely on your nose!
F2
Do not touch them! Table one has hot mint tea, black tea, and warm plates ready.
M2
{F3} is at the walnut piano, and both Room Two and Six guests are smiling!
F1
We actually pulled off a six-hour celebration in a hundred and eighty minutes!
F2
Listen—do you hear the municipal clock tower chiming three up {STREET}?
M2
One chime, two chimes, three chimes... and wait, a car door just closed outside!
F1
Someone just rang the brass gate bell twice—that is the signal from the brothers!
F2
Look through the archway: {M4} is carrying a battered brown leather suitcase!
M2
And walking beside {M3} with a silver walking stick and a wide straw hat...
F1
Remember to lift the iron gate handle slightly first, {M2}, and smile!
M2
Welcome back to {SHOW}, my friend—thirty summers to the very week!
scenes.outro: Three chimes ring out, the gate latch lifts smoothly, and after thirty summers the mapmaker of Room 8 steps back under the courtyard tree! End of Episode 5—see you in the Season 3 finale!
